name: Humbug
description: Humbug is a minimalist 18th-century trick-taking game for two players, representing the simplest possible adaptation of Whist. It is unique because both players are dealt the entire deck, making it a game of perfect information (after the initial overview) and a rigorous test of memory and card counting.

overview.description: Humbug is a minimalist 18th-century trick-taking game for two players, representing the simplest possible adaptation of Whist. It is unique because both players are dealt the entire deck, making it a game of perfect information (after the initial overview) and a rigorous test of memory and card counting.

history.origins: Documented in London publications as early as 1793 (e.g., The Sporting Magazine). It was designed as a high-stakes gambling game for two people who wanted the rigor of Whist without needing partners.
timeline: 1790s: First mentioned in British sporting journals.
19th Century: Gradually replaced by German Whist, which introduced hidden information.
Present: Studied by game historians as a precursor to modern 2-player trick-taking games.
history.cultural: Often played in clubs and informal settings for high stakes due to its clinical, non-random nature.
history.evolution: The game's 'Humbug' name likely refers to the deceptive nature of lead strategies in a game where both players know the full deck state.

setup.players: Exactly two players. Humbug was designed as a high-stakes two-hand whist variant for two people who wanted the rigor of Whist without partners; it is documented in London publications from the 1790s (e.g. The Sporting Magazine).
setup.dealing: Deal all 52 cards, one at a time. The final card (belonging to the dealer) is turned up to determine the Trump suit. Both players then layout their hand face-up by suit to see the complete game state.

rules.objective: Win more than 26 tricks to be the winner of the deal.
rules.gameplay:
1. Non-dealer leads the first card.
2. Standard Whist rules: Must follow suit if possible.
3. Highest card of the suit led wins the trick, unless a trump is played.
4. Winner of the trick leads the next.
5. **Perfect Information**: Since all cards are dealt, players know exactly what the opponent holds at all times.
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Humbug.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: The game is scored by the number of tricks won.
Winning condition: Win more than 26 tricks to be the winner of the deal.

strategy.basic: Card Counting: Since you know every card your opponent has, the game becomes a puzzle. Identify which suits you dominate and lead them early to draw out trumps.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Management: If you have the higher trumps, use them to kill your opponent's Aces in their long suits.
strategy.advanced: Endplay positioning: Force your opponent into a 'Throw-in' where they must lead into your winning cards in the final few tricks.
tips: Always track the remainders of the trump suit.
In a game of 52 cards, the distribution is key. If you have 10 hearts, your opponent only has 3; use this to exhaust them.
